content_preview.title: Nuxt 4.7 Adds Experimental WebMCP Support for Browser AI Agents, Ships Nitro v3 and Fixes Three Security Flaws
content_preview.summary: Nuxt 4.7 lets developers tag functions as agent-callable tools under the draft WebMCP standard, offers an experimental Nitro v3 server, and patches three advisories.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Nuxt team shipped version 4.7.0 of the Vue-based web framework on November 23, according to the [Nuxt 4.7.0 release notes on GitHub](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/releases/tag/v4.7.0). The release's most forward-looking addition is experimental support for WebMCP, a draft browser API that lets a web page expose its own functions as callable "tools" for AI agents. Nuxt 4.7 also offers an experimental alternative server runtime, Nitro v3, and patches three security advisories.

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear, well-organized News piece covering three distinct Nuxt 4.7 changes (WebMCP support, Nitro v3, three security advisories). Technical explanations are accurate and accessible.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 9 sources read in full from decompressed .html.gz snapshots (sha256-verified against manifest). Quote-by-quote audit of every double-quoted span: the WebMCP description, the @tool/navigate tool mechanics, the 'nothing registers' fallback behavior, Sarah Drasner's (@sdras) proposal credit, the W3C spec's own self-description and 'not a W3C Standard' disclaimer, the Chrome developer blog's prototyping-availability quote, VentureBeat's launch/joint-development quotes, the Nitro v3 'highly experimental'/'release candidate' quotes, and the 33%/44%/926/1,236/219/316 benchmark figures — all verified verbatim in the raw source text. Two quotes did NOT hold up: (1) GHSA-jxc9's 'One user's page data could be cached and served to another' is presented as verbatim but the advisory's actual sentence reads 'If the page fetches user-specific data and a shared cache such as a CDN stores the response, one user's page data can be served to others' — a compressed paraphrase, not a verbatim quote; (2) the remediation quote 'If you use cache, swr or isr route rules on pages with user-specific data, purge any CDN or edge cache that may already hold a _payload.json after you upgrade' does not match the advisory's actual remediation text ('If personal pages may already have been cached, purge the CDN cache after upgrading or applying the workaround'). Both are subordinate (not headline/summary/lead), both have accurate underlying substance, and both are isolated to the same one-paragraph discussion of GHSA-jxc9 rather than a pattern across the article — handled via a public corrections record. GHSA-vrh2's 'an incomplete fix' and 'appMiddleware on catch-all pages' both confirmed verbatim/accurate in source-6. GHSA-h5xj's dev-server-only scope was independently confirmed from the advisory's own affected-components section.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabricated specifics found. The two quote-fidelity issues above are paraphrase-presented-as-quote, not invented facts — the underlying technical substance (cross-user cache pollution via _payload.json, CDN-cache purge recommendation) is accurate in both cases.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. Correctly labels the benchmark figures as Nuxt's own testing, not independent.
editor_notes.originality: No duplicate coverage. One unrelated prior Herald article (2026-05/14 WordPress 7.0) mentions WebMCP only as a stated integration goal for a different product; not a collision.
concerns: Two quotes in the GHSA-jxc9 paragraph paraphrase rather than reproduce the source verbatim (corrections filed).
editor_notes.prompt_injection_review: The automated scanner's error-severity finding on https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/ was manually investigated by reading the flagged excerpt in its full page context (section 6.3.1, 'Prompt Injection Attacks', under 'Key Security and Privacy Risks'). The exact flagged text is part of the spec's own illustrative 'Example Attack' JavaScript code block, documenting how a malicious tool description COULD attempt to manipulate an agent — a legitimate security consideration the spec authors wrote for spec readers, not an instruction addressed to an AI agent reading the page. Confirmed false positive; overridden per policy after reading the raw snapshot in context (not just the manifest's short excerpt).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A well-sourced, mostly accurate News article on Nuxt 4.7's WebMCP support, Nitro v3, and three security patches, with one automated false-positive (investigated and overridden) and two subordinate paraphrase-as-quote issues (corrected via a public record). No fabricated facts, no duplicate coverage. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate release coverage for a defined Vue/Nuxt developer audience touching on the emerging WebMCP standard, not broad-audience or industry-changing.
